messages:
maria: Heads-up — retention-controller alerted on sustained spike from a handful of tenants, exporters to Tempo/Splunk are retrying and backing up into the queue. Can we triage routing/TTL quick fixes?
ashok: I’m looking. initial read: 6 tenants at ~4x normal span rate, a few 503s from tempo-eu. seems like exporter backpressure not surfaced as a throttling decision.
kai: @ashok do we have per-tenant routing rules that can lower retention/TTL automatically when exporter errors happen?
ashok: not currently. we only have global fallback order + capacity heuristics. Per-tenant TTL shim would help.
tempo-bot: export failure: tempo-eu returned 503 (rate_limited) for batch_id=0x3f4a, retry_after=30s
june: If we add a temporary TTL override for noisy tenants we should also avoid changing persisted retention config. maybe a runtime "shim" that applies for N hours.
maria: Agreed. Proposal: on exporter error spike, mark tenant as "throttled" and route to lower-retention sinks or drop non-critical spans for 1h, with exponential backoff.
kai: rough config sketch:```yaml
routing:
  policy: "error-driven-tiering"
  transient_ttl_shim:
    enabled: true
    window: 1h
    threshold_events_per_min: 1000
    actions:
      - lower_ttl: 24h
      - reduce_sample_rate: 0.1
      - fallback_sinks: ["tempo-lowprio","splunk-delq"]
```
ashok: that looks reasonable. implementation notes: need to emit events so console shows "tenant X in transient_ttl_shim" and a metric for shim_count. Also must expose which spans are dropped for SLO traces.
maria: UX: console should show active throttles and a rollback button + audit log. For rollouts we need a canary on small subset first.
june: Concern: lowering TTL might break customers expecting long trace retention. we should only apply to tenants that exceed rate thresholds or are in "noisy" group. keep a whitelist/blacklist.
sre-bot: incident note created: INC-2024-099 — exporter-queue-pressure. linked: https://internal/incidents/INC-2024-099 :clipboard: 
kai: ops-level detail: exporter queue sizes spike when `max_queue_size` is hit and we don't apply backpressure upstream. two mitigations: 1) circuit-break exporter (fast-fail upstream) 2) transient TTL shim + sampler tweak. prefer both.
nashok: implement plan: (A) add metrics + console widget (kai) (B) add runtime transient TTL shim (ashok) (C) add policy to route to lower-cost sinks (maria) (D) update runbooks & incident playbook (june).
maria: timeline? this afternoon for metrics + alert tweak, patch for TTL shim in next 2 days, dashboard updates by EOD tomorrow.
kai: will push a dashboard prototype now. ping me if you want to test with a noisy tenant. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks — keep thread updated. if tempo-eu keeps returning 503s we’ll flip fallback routing to splunk for the noisy tenants. :eyes:
